newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania police break up rally in Tirana.
newsitem.headline: Albania police break up rally in Tirana.

text.p: Albanian police broke up an anti-government rally at a soccer stadium in Tirana on Wednesday, punching and jostling demonstrators, witnesses said.
The rally called by an independent trade union headed by Hazem Hajdari, one of the leaders of the 1990 anti-communist revolt, was dispersed before speakers could address a crowd of around 200 people.
The crowd had gathered on one side of soccer field when 40 to 50 police officers arrived and began pushing the people back to prevent the rally going ahead.
When some refused to move on, police became more aggressive and punched the most reluctant. A group of women set upon police officers to stop them dragging one man into a police van.
"Look at them, and they call this a democracy," one woman shouted as police vans sped on streets around the soccer stadium.

Many of those in the field were investors who had put money in a failed pyramid investment scheme. Albania has been hit by a wave of violence over the past three weeks since the investment scams began to crumble, leaving thousands penniless.
